reflections.body: Ok so I'm here porque my nephew said this app helps with organization. That's it. Necesito un poco de organización, that's all. Between the shop y everybody calling me for todo, my head is like a pile of party balloons someone let go. Nothing serious. Estoy bien.

Today: reordered the inflatables, fixed the register, took my cousin's kid to the dentist because nobody else could. Normal Tuesday. La gente me llama cuando algo se rompe. I'm the one who fixes. Es lo que hago.

Valentina keeps asking me qué necesito YO. Funny question. Nadie me lo pregunta así. I said I need the tent order to come in on time jaja. She didn't laugh. She just waited. I don't know what she wants me to say.

Slept four hours. The Ramírez quinceañera pickup was at 6am. My back hurts. Pero estoy bien, always. I fixed a broken chair leg with a clamp and a prayer and it held. Mis manos saben lo que hacen aunque el resto de mí no.

Mi hermana llamó domingo like always. She asked how I was and I said 'bien bien todo bien' before she even finished. Then she said 'Rosa, dime la verdad' and I changed the subject to her kids. It's easier to carry hers than to open mine.

Un poco de organización, I keep telling myself. But last night I sat in the shop after closing y no me quería ir a casa. Empty store, all the piñatas hanging like little ghosts. I felt like I disappear behind that counter. Como si yo fuera parte del inventario.

Valentina asked about my childhood and I don't know why but I started talking about my mother's shifts. Ella trabajaba de noche en el hospital. I was the oldest of six. Yo era la mamá chiquita. I made the lunches, I did the braids, I stayed up when the baby cried. No había espacio para que yo necesitara nada.

Couldn't stop thinking about that. La mamá chiquita. I never called myself that before yesterday. Seven years old y ya estaba planchando uniformes. Needing something was a luxury nobody in that house could afford. So I just… stopped needing. Y todavía.

The course thing — Boundaries Without Guilt. I laughed at the title. Fronteras sin culpa? For me those two words don't go together. Every time I say no to someone la culpa me come viva. But I started module one anyway.

A regular, doña Carmen, brought me pastelillos today just because. Sin razón. Just because. I almost cried at the register como una boba. These people treat me like familia. Maybe I let them closer than I let my own blood, isn't that something.

Fought with myself all week. My employee Yesenia asked for more hours and part of me wanted to say sí, take the whole weekend, but then who watches everything? Si yo suelto, todo se cae. That's the fear. If I stop holding it, it all comes down.

Worksheet Valentina sent — the one about 'what am I afraid happens if I ask.' I wrote: they'll see I'm not enough. Then I stared at it. No sabía que eso estaba ahí abajo. That I think asking = being a burden = not being enough. Ay. Ese fue un golpe.

I did it. Le dije a Yesenia she could cover Saturday. Todo el sábado. My hands were sweating like I was doing something illegal jaja. But she said 'claro Rosa, yo te cubro, descansa.' Descansa. Nobody tells me to rest.

Saturday off and I didn't know what to do with my body. I kept picking up the phone to check on the shop. Then I put it down. Then I texted mi hermana — not to fix anything, just to say 'te extraño.' She called back crying happy. We talked an hour. No apagué ningún fuego. Solo hablamos.

The shop didn't burn down while I was gone. Everything was fine. Yesenia even sold the big helium package I always mess up the pricing on. So maybe 'todo se cae' isn't as true as la nena adentro de mí believes. Maybe things hold without me white-knuckling them.

Bad week. Back to old ways. A supplier canceled and I took the whole thing on my shoulders, no dormí, snapped at everybody, said estoy bien like a broken record. Valentina says the old pattern comes back when I'm stressed. Sí. Como un perro que vuelve a su casa vieja.

Talked it through. I noticed something — cuando algo se rompe afuera, I run to fix it so I don't have to feel what's roto adentro. Taking on other people's crises is how I skip my own. That one landed heavy. I've been doing that my whole life.

Mi hermana asked me for help this time — with a family thing back in Bayamón — and I noticed I felt USEFUL, important, needed. And then I noticed: that feeling is the trap. If being needed is the only way I feel worth something, then I can never ask, porque pedir me quita el único valor que creo tener.

Third worksheet done. The one mapping who I let carry things for me. The list was almost empty al principio. Then I added Yesenia. Doña Carmen. Mi hermana. Small. Pero es un comienzo. La lista está creciendo.

I said it out loud in session and it felt like taking off a coat I've worn 40 años: pedir ayuda no me hace débil. Asking for help doesn't make me weak. My voice shook saying it. Pero lo dije. And a little part of me almost believed it.

Practicing. I asked my nephew to help me carry the folding tables instead of doing it sola y matándome la espalda. He said 'obvio tía.' Obvio. Like it was nothing. For him it WAS nothing. All these years I thought asking was such a big weight to put on people. Maybe it's a gift I never let anybody give me.

Boundaries course, module four. Learning to say 'no puedo esta vez' without the twenty-minute apology after. I told a customer I couldn't do a same-day rush order. Just… no. La culpa vino pero más chiquita this time. Más manejable.

Domingo con mi hermana. This time when she asked 'cómo estás de verdad' I didn't deflect. I said 'cansada, pero trabajando en eso.' Tired but working on it. She got quiet and said 'me alegra que te estás cuidando.' Nobody's ever been glad I'm taking care of ME.

I catch myself now. Someone asks how I am, 'estoy bien' flies out automática like always — pero ahora lo oigo. I hear it leave my mouth like a little bird I trained too well. Yesterday I caught it and added 'bueno, más o menos, ha sido una semana larga.' Progress isn't silence anymore.

The shop feels different or maybe I feel different behind it. I'm not disappearing anymore, estoy aquí, present, a person and not just a counter with hands. Yesenia's basically co-managing now. I go home at a normal hour. Ceno. Sometimes I do nothing. Nothing! Y no se cayó nada.

Said 'estoy bien' to doña Carmen out of pure habit today and then I laughed out loud right there at the register. She goes '¿de qué te ríes?' and I said 'de mí misma, Carmen, de una costumbre vieja.' She laughed too. It's still there, the reflex. But now it makes me laugh instead of hide.

Nine months. La mamá chiquita is still in me, siempre va a estar — she raised six kids, she deserves respect. But I'm learning she doesn't have to run everything anymore. Puedo pedir. Puedo descansar. Puedo necesitar. And the world keeps spinning, la tienda keeps its lights on, y mi hermana llama los domingos. No estoy sola. Nunca lo estuve tanto como creía.

messages.body: Hola Valentina, solo quiero un poco de organización I think. My days are all over the place. Nothing major.
Bienvenida, Rosa. We can absolutely work on organization. I'm curious though — when everything's organized, what would that free you up to do for yourself?
Jaja para mí? No sé. Nadie me pregunta eso. Probably just fix more stuff faster lol
That phrase you used — 'la mamá chiquita' — stayed with me. Would you be open to writing more about her this week?
Sí. It's weird, I never thought about that little girl como una persona separate from me. Voy a intentar.
Empecé el curso de boundaries. The title made me roll my eyes ngl. Fronteras sin culpa, en mi casa eso no existe 😅
Roll your eyes all you want — just keep going. The guilt is the part we're actually working on, not the boundary itself.
Ok I need to tell someone. Le di el sábado entero a Yesenia. A DAY OFF. Estoy nerviosa como si fuera a explotar la tienda 😬
This is huge, Rosa. Notice everything you feel Saturday — the urge to check in, the discomfort of rest. Don't fix it. Just watch it.
The shop survived 😭 y hablé con mi hermana una hora entera. No fires. Just talking. I forgot you could just… talk.
Bad week. Un proveedor me canceló y volví a lo de siempre, no dormí, cargando todo yo. Me siento como si retrocedí todo.
You didn't go backward, Rosa. You returned to an old path under stress — and this time you NOTICED it. That noticing is brand new. That's the work.
Ay. Ok. Puesto así se siente distinto. Gracias. Un perro que vuelve a su casa vieja pero esta vez sabe que no es su casa ya.
You said something powerful — that being needed feels like your only worth. What if your worth isn't in what you carry for others at all?
Esa pregunta me tiene despierta. Si no soy la que carga todo, entonces quién soy? Da miedo. Pero también... alivio?
Valentina lo dije en voz alta hoy. Pedir ayuda no me hace débil. Me temblaba la voz pero lo dije 🥹
I felt that through the screen. Say it again this week when it's easier, and again when it's hard. Let it become yours.
Told a customer no rush order. Just NO. Sin el sermón de disculpas de veinte minutos jaja. La culpa vino pero más chiquita.
Smaller guilt, cleaner no. That's exactly it. You're building the muscle.
Le dije la verdad a mi hermana el domingo. 'Cansada pero trabajando en eso.' She said she's glad I'm taking care of me. Lloré un poquito 🥲
How's the 'estoy bien' reflex doing these days?
Todavía sale solita! Pero ahora la oigo salir. And I catch her and add the real answer after. It's like I trained a bird too well and now I'm untraining her lol
Se me salió 'estoy bien' con doña Carmen y me reí sola en el register 😂 She asked what was funny and I told her the truth — una costumbre vieja.
From hiding to laughing. That's not a small thing, Rosa. That's the whole shift, right there at the register.

notes.body: Intake. Rosa arrives framing everything as a logistics problem — 'un poco de organización.' Classic over-functioner: presents with the symptom that keeps her useful, deflects any question back onto family. Every 'how are you' returns 'estoy bien.' Note the language pattern: English for the practical/transactional, Spanish surfacing only when something tender slips through. That's my map — follow the Spanish.

First real crack. She named 'yo era la mamá chiquita' — parentified eldest of six, mother on night shifts, needing was structurally impossible in that home. The wound (I-must-not-need) has a clear origin now. Notice she describes it in Spanish and almost tearfully. Not pushing; letting her circle back on her own terms. Sister in Bayamón is a live resource — she's just never let it flow toward herself.

Predictable stress-relapse after supplier cancellation — reverted to white-knuckling, sleeplessness, 'estoy bien.' Reframed as return-to-old-path WITH new awareness, not regression. She metabolized this well ('el perro que vuelve a su casa vieja pero sabe que no es su casa'). Her own metaphors are doing the therapeutic lifting now. Underlying belief exposed: being-needed = only source of worth. That's the next layer.

Milestone. 'Pedir ayuda no me hace débil' spoken aloud, voice shaking. The core belief (asking = burden = not-enough) is loosening, not yet integrated — she 'almost' believed it. Behavioral evidence accumulating: delegated a full weekend, asked nephew for help, honest with sister. Boundaries course reinforcing. Keep grounding the cognitive shift in the body wins so it doesn't stay abstract.

Near end of tenure. The 'estoy bien' reflex persists but has transformed function — from shield to self-aware humor. She catches it, laughs, corrects. That's integration behaving exactly as it should: the old pattern isn't erased, it's held with awareness and warmth. She's present behind the counter now instead of disappearing into it. Yesenia co-managing, normal hours, resting without collapse. Recommend maintenance cadence. Strong prognosis.
